title: Uncontrollable
subtitle: The Threat of Artificial Superintelligence and the Race to Save the World
pitch: Written for people with no technical background, it explains what AI is, why superintelligence could slip out of control, and what ordinary citizens can do.
toc_note: I could not find a full chapter list from a library or publisher page, so this guide follows the book's three parts as described in published reviews.

chapters.g: An overview of the AI landscape for beginners, with clear definitions of AI, AGI and ASI, and how image and language models work.
The longest part. Why we do not fully understand what happens inside AI systems, and the different ways superintelligence could become a threat.
The shortest part: practical steps for governments, companies and citizens to make a safer future with AI.

ideas: You do not need a technical background to understand AI risk.
We do not fully understand what is happening inside AI systems.
Citizens have a role in demanding safety.

args.a: Superintelligence may arrive soon and could be uncontrollable.
args.c: Some reviewers felt the book uses a fairly low bar for what counts as superintelligence.

questions: Which analogy in the book helped you most?
What is one thing a citizen in India could do after reading it?

quiz.q: Who is this book mainly written for?
quiz.w: It uses analogies and everyday examples.
Most of the book explains the risks.
